gen-gf-baumans-gf-rokkitt: Bookish and slightly stout, Rokkitt reads like a well-worn paperback with its wide-open curves. Baumans stands over it with one unvarying line weight, so the heading looks stamped while the text below feels set by hand.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-sanchez: Sanchez reads with a dignified, bookish gait, its curves opened wide like calipers. But Baumans draws every letter without a single thick or thin part, so enlarging the body would bring the two much closer.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-solway: Authoritative from the first word, Baumans cuts its letters like stencil work, every stroke at a single flat thickness. Solway follows in a classic serif that stays bookish and welcoming.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-yuji-boku: Stamped, stern, and unmistakable. Baumans draws every stroke at one thickness, while Yuji Boku answers in a dignified text serif with wide-open curves, so the page gets muscle on top and an editorial voice beneath.
gen-gf-baumans-nunito-sans: One flat line weight runs through every glyph of Baumans, giving it a stamped, commanding look. Yet Nunito Sans softens the page below it, a plain sans whose open-mouthed small letters keep long paragraphs gentle.
gen-gf-bellota-dm-sans: Bellota draws its letters like a marker tip, with s ends hanging far from the spine. DM Sans is the friendlier one, with wide-set terminals that make it the better fit for ordinary text, while Bellota is the one that grabs attention.
gen-gf-bellota-fs-paquito: Bent-pipe lettering, confident and a little odd. Bellota keeps every stroke at constant width, and Paquito, a serif with barely any gap between x-height and caps, reads as a compact, approachable block of text.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-aleo: Bellota opens with zero stroke contrast and hanging s ends. Aleo is a dignified, classic serif whose counters let the eye slip in and out, so making it a touch smaller than the heading suits it.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-almendra-sc: Bellota looks cut from strips of equal width, with s ends hanging far from its spine. Almendra SC is a classic serif with mouths left open on c, e, and a, and it holds up best a little below the heading's size.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-antic-slab: Pipe-like strokes meet slab squareness here. Bellota hangs the ends of its s far from the spine, and Antic Slab keeps its round bowls uniform in a dignified, editorial classic serif, which is where the pair is strongest.
